news.headline: MicroCap Opportunities: 'First Two Claires and the Reimbursement Clock'
news.summary: A detailed post-Q2 breakdown notes both installed Claire systems are S-Series conversions at Intermountain's LDS Hospital and American Fork rather than net-new customers, leaving the site count stuck at 22 and producing no upfront capital-sale revenue. It frames Q2's US$503K revenue (all legacy), the 28% year-over-year opex cut to US$3.1M and US$6.4M cash with roughly 12 months of runway as a race between the commercial ramp and the CMS reimbursement clock.

news.headline: Perimeter Announces Preliminary Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results
news.summary: Q2 2026 revenue was about US$503K, all recurring (S-Series consumables, system leases, maintenance), essentially flat versus US$506K a year ago, while operating expenses fell 28% year-over-year to US$3.1M and the net loss narrowed to US$2.6M from US$3.9M in Q2 2025. Cash stood at US$6.4M at June 30, and the release highlighted the first two Claire placements as S-Series replacements at two top-tier hospitals.

news.headline: Q2 2026 earnings call: 2-3x revenue growth target held, funnel 'in flux', HCPCS application under CMS review
news.summary: CEO Adrian Mendes confirmed only two Claire systems are commercially installed - both conversions of existing S-Series customers - with the installed base unchanged at 22 sites, and declined to quantify the sales funnel, calling it 'in flux' as hospital AI review committees push some deals toward 2027. CFO Sara Brien reiterated roughly 12 months of runway on the US$6.4M cash balance, and management confirmed the HCPCS coding application filed with CMS in June is under review, with first Medicare claims expected in Q1 2027.

news.headline: Intermountain Health Deploys Claire OCT System to Aid Breast Cancer Surgery
news.summary: Coverage of the go-live carried the first surgeon feedback: Intermountain LDS Hospital breast surgeon Dr. Teresa Reading said Claire was 'incredibly simple to incorporate into my workflow' and that the AI quickly directed her attention to specific areas. The article restates the core clinical case - roughly one in five breast-conserving surgery patients needs a second operation because residual cancer was missed.

news.headline: Intermountain Health Brings Perimeter's Claire to the Operating Room, a Landmark in Breast Cancer Surgery Using AI
news.summary: Intermountain Health became the first U.S. health system to commercially deploy Claire for real-time margin assessment in breast-conserving surgery, going live at LDS Hospital and American Fork Hospital in Utah under the systemwide agreement signed in January 2026. It is the first named commercial placement since the March 2026 FDA PMA approval, and the shares jumped roughly 11% on the news.

news.headline: Perimeter Schedules Second Quarter 2026 Conference Call and Discloses Final LIFE Offering Tranche
news.summary: Alongside scheduling the August 20 Q2 call, Perimeter clarified that it had issued a final 1,955,500 units at C$0.35 on May 8, 2026 for additional gross proceeds of C$684,425, taking the listed-issuer-financing-exemption offering to its full 21,489,000 units and C$7,521,150. The company also paid C$47,910 in additional cash commissions and issued 136,885 broker warrants.

catalysts.label: Roll-out across the wider Intermountain Health network
catalysts.detail: Claire is live at only two Intermountain hospitals (LDS Hospital and American Fork Hospital) despite a systemwide agreement covering a much larger network. Expansion to further Intermountain sites would show the flagship customer scales instead of stalling at a two-site footprint, and would lift per-procedure consumable revenue, which is the recurring part of the model. Because these are S-Series conversions, incremental sites are also the fastest route to actual volume growth.

catalysts.label: Q3 2026 results - first full quarter of Claire commercialization
catalysts.detail: The Q3 print, typically released in November (Q2 preliminary results came on August 20), is the first full reporting period after the August Intermountain go-live. It is the first look at Claire-related recurring revenue and gross margin against the roughly US$2M annualized S-Series base, and the next hard update on cash burn and runway. No date has been announced yet; Perimeter usually schedules the call about a week in advance.

catalysts.label: First net-new Claire placement outside the legacy base
catalysts.detail: Only two Claire systems are commercially installed, both conversions of existing S-Series customers, on a flat installed base of 22 sites. Conversions carry no upfront capital-sale revenue, so a genuinely new hospital system signing - rather than another legacy swap - is the clearest proof that the Intermountain deal is repeatable. Management said late-stage pipeline opportunities exist but would not size the funnel, citing hospital AI review committees as the bottleneck.

catalysts.label: CMS HCPCS code decision for Claire
catalysts.detail: Perimeter filed its HCPCS coding application with CMS in June 2026 and management confirmed on the August 20 call that it is under review. A June filing normally carries a January 1, 2027 effective date, with an outside chance of October 1, 2026; management guided to first Medicare and Medicare Advantage claims in Q1 2027. A dedicated code is the precondition for hospital billing and for commercial payers opening medical policy reviews, and is the single biggest structural unlock for the adoption curve.

catalysts.label: Delivery on the 2-3x FY2026 revenue growth target
catalysts.detail: Management reaffirmed guidance of 2-3x revenue growth for 2026 but conceded that hospital AI review committees could push deals into 2027. With H1 revenue under US$0.9M against FY2025 revenue of about US$2.3M, the target implies an extremely back-loaded Q4 built on capital sales that have not yet been signed, making the year-end update a hard test of the commercial ramp and of management credibility.

catalysts.label: Next financing round
catalysts.detail: Cash stood at US$6.4M on June 30 with management projecting roughly 12 months of runway, following the C$7.52M LIFE offering (21,489,000 units at C$0.35, final tranche closed May 8) and C$6.04M of convertible debentures closed in June. With the shares around C$0.30, well below that C$0.35 issue price, a further raise is likely and would be materially more dilutive unless a new customer signing or the HCPCS code re-rates the stock first.

pulse: The company has gone quiet since the August 20 Q2 print - the IR press-release feed shows nothing in September, and there was no news on September 5-7 - leaving the stock parked around C$0.30 for a market cap near C$46M, versus roughly C$0.40 at the mid-August Intermountain peak and a 52-week range of C$0.17-C$0.72. The setup is unchanged: Claire is the only FDA PMA-approved AI-enabled breast-margin device and is now live in real operating rooms at Intermountain's LDS and American Fork hospitals, but both installs are conversions of existing S-Series customers on a flat 22-site base, Q2 revenue of US$503K was entirely legacy, and management would not quantify the funnel beyond calling it 'in flux'. With US$6.4M cash and about 12 months of runway against a C$1.54 analyst target that assumes the ramp works, the two things to watch are the CMS HCPCS code filed in June (first Medicare claims guided to Q1 2027) and a first genuinely new hospital signing; the November Q3 print is the next scheduled checkpoint.
